hypothesis: Pitch-level Bernoulli labels are too noisy for the small seasonal transfer problem. A leave-one-row-out empirical-Bayes hierarchy over completed historical pitcher-season, batter-season, count and hand contexts supplies a stable probability target. A CatBoost Brier regressor can learn this probability surface from exact-C row features without inspecting any validation or test aggregate.

novelty_audit.distinct_from_e14: E14 exposes frozen and as-of features but still fits hard pitch labels. This experiment changes the training estimand to a completed-history hierarchical probability.
novelty_audit.distinct_from_teacher_runs: Earlier teacher experiments used model predictions or TrackMan physics as soft targets. This target is an analytic leave-one-out hierarchy made only from official completed-history outcomes.
novelty_audit.distinct_from_hierarchical_features: Earlier H1/H2/H4 paths supplied target-rate features while retaining hard labels. Here the hierarchy is the supervised target and is not available as an inference feature.
